items.prompt: Yesterday we ___ football in the park.

options.why: Play is for now or every day. Yesterday is in the past.
Will play is for the future.
Playing needs a helper word, like were playing.

hints: Look for the word that tells you when.
Yesterday means the past.
Many past tense verbs end in -ed.
items.explanation: Yesterday tells us it happened in the past, so we use played.

items.prompt: Tomorrow I ___ visit my grandma.

options.why: Am needs an -ing word, like I am visiting.

hints: Look for the word that tells you when.
Tomorrow means the future.
Which word can go in front of visit to show the future?
items.explanation: Tomorrow is in the future. We use will with a verb to show the future: I will visit.

items.prompt: Sort the sentences into past, present and future.
hints: Look at the verb in each sentence.
Words ending in -ed, and words like went, are often past. Will shows the future.
Start with We will swim. Which group does will belong in?
items.explanation: Walked, sang and went are past. Runs, is eating and cooks are present. Will swim, will read and will rain are future.

items.prompt:
Write the past tense of eat.
Last night, Rani ___ rice and fish.
hints: Last night is in the past.
Eat does not take -ed. It changes to a new word.
Say it aloud: Today I eat. Yesterday I ...?
items.explanation: Eat is an irregular verb. Its past tense is ate.

items.prompt: Match each verb to its past tense.
hints: These verbs do not take -ed.
Say each one aloud: Today I go. Yesterday I ...
Start with see. What did you do yesterday with your eyes?
items.explanation: These verbs are irregular, so the past tense changes. Go becomes went, swim becomes swam, see becomes saw, take becomes took and fly becomes flew.

items.prompt:
Write the past tense of stop.
The bus ___ at the school gate.
hints: Stop is a regular verb, so it takes -ed.
Stop has one short vowel and ends in one consonant.
Think about how hop becomes hopped.
items.explanation: Stop ends in one consonant after a short vowel, so we double the p and add -ed: stopped.

items.prompt: Which sentence is about the future?

options.why: Has started means it already happened.

hints: The future is something that has not happened yet.
Look for a word that shows the future.
Read each sentence and ask: has this happened yet?
items.explanation: Will start shows something that is going to happen. That is the future tense.

items.prompt:
Write sleep in the present tense.
Every morning, my cat ___ in the sun.
hints: Every morning tells us it happens again and again.
Use the present tense for things that happen often.
My cat is one animal. What do you add to the verb after he, she or it?
items.explanation: Every morning shows something that happens often, so we use the present tense. With one cat, we add -s: sleeps.

items.prompt: The baby ___ when the dog barked.

options.why: Cry is the present tense. Barked tells us it is the past.
When a word ends in a consonant and y, the y changes to i before -ed.

hints: Barked tells you the sentence is in the past.
Cry ends in a consonant and then y.
Think about how carry changes when you add -ed.
items.explanation: Barked is in the past, so the baby cried. Cry changes y to i before -ed.

items.prompt: Which sentence is all in the past tense?

options.text: I woke up and ate my breakfast.
I woke up and eat my breakfast.
options.why: Eat is the present tense. It should be ate.

options.text: I wake up and ate my breakfast.
options.why: Wake is the present tense. It should be woke.

options.text: I will wake up and ate my breakfast.
options.why: Will wake is the future tense.

hints: Find the two verbs in each sentence.
Both verbs must be in the past.
Check the first verb, then check the verb after and.
items.explanation: Woke and ate are both past tense verbs, so that sentence is all in the past.

items.prompt:
Change the verbs to the past tense.
Today I swim, then I write a story.
Yesterday I ___, then I ___ a story.
hints: Both verbs are irregular. They do not take -ed.
Say it aloud: Today I swim. Yesterday I ...
Do swim first. Listen for the vowel sound that changes.
items.explanation: Swim becomes swam and write becomes wrote. These are irregular past tense verbs.

items.prompt:
How many verbs are in the wrong tense?
Last Sunday, we go to the beach. We built a sandcastle and will eat ice cream.

options.why: Look at go and will eat again. Last Sunday was in the past.
There is more than one verb in the wrong tense.
Built is correct. It is the past tense of build.

hints: Last Sunday tells you everything happened in the past.
Find every verb: go, built and will eat.
Check each verb. Is it in the past tense?
items.explanation: Go should be went, and will eat should be ate. Built is already in the past, so 2 verbs are wrong.

items.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence about the future.
hints: The sentence starts with a word that tells you when.
The future needs the helper word will.
The last word has a full stop and names the place.
items.explanation: Tomorrow we will visit the zoo. Will before the doing word shows the future.
items.answer: Tomorrow we will visit the zoo.

items.prompt: Tomorrow we ___ to the museum.
hints: Tomorrow means the future.
The future often uses the helper word will.
Which choice has will?
items.explanation: Will go shows something that has not happened yet.

items.prompt: Which sentence is in the future?
hints: Future means it has not happened yet.
Look for the word will.
It comes before the verb.
items.explanation: I will go to school. is in the future.

items.prompt: Yesterday we ___ rice.
hints: Yesterday tells us the time.
It is in the past.
Eat has a special past.
items.explanation: Ate is the past of eat.

items.prompt: Tomorrow, I ___ my aunt.
hints: Tomorrow has not come yet.
Use will with the verb.
It is the future.
items.explanation: Will visit is in the future.

items.prompt: Which sentence is in the present?
hints: Present happens now or every day.
Look for the time words.
Every day is a clue.
items.explanation: She sings every day. is in the present.

items.prompt: Sort the sentences by tense.
hints: Look at the verb.
will shows the future.
ed shows the past.
items.explanation: Walked and played are past. Walk and play are present. Will walk and will play are future.

items.prompt: Write the past tense. Yesterday Dad ___ rice. (cook)
hints: Yesterday means the past.
Add ed.
Cook plus ed.
items.explanation: Dad cooked rice yesterday.

items.prompt: Write the future tense. Next week we ___ the zoo. (visit)
hints: Next week has not come yet.
Use two words.
The first word is will.
items.explanation: We will visit the zoo next week.

items.prompt: Match each time word to a sentence.
hints: Think about when.
Yesterday is the past.
Tomorrow is the future.
items.explanation: Each time word fits one tense.

items.prompt: Last night, I ___ a film.
hints: Last night is in the past.
Use the form with ed.
Not will.
items.explanation: Watched is in the past.

items.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.
hints: The sentence starts with We.
Will comes before the verb.
It ends with a full stop.
items.explanation: We will plant a tree.

items.prompt: Which sentence has the wrong tense?
hints: Check the time word with the verb.
Yesterday is in the past.
Will is for the future.
items.explanation: Yesterday needs a past verb, not will go.

options.text: Tomorrow I will go to the park.
Yesterday I will go to the park.
Last week I went to the park.
Today I go to the park.

items.prompt: We ___ to the beach on Sunday. Today is Monday. Which verb fits?
hints: Today is Monday.
Sunday was the day before.
It is in the past.
items.explanation: Sunday has already passed, so we need the past: went.

items.prompt: Complete the table.
hints: Most verbs add ed in the past.
Sing and eat change their whole word.
Walk and jump add ed.
items.explanation: Walk becomes walked and jump becomes jumped.
head: Now
